author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only veterinarians holding it. Whole-name, case-insensitive match; blank is ignored; no on-page control.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty named in the address, when the paged directory is opened, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, a page at a time
given a specialty named in the address, when the machine-readable list is requested, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are returned
given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either form is requested, then it matches
given the start of a specialty name rather than the whole name, when either form is requested, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested, then it succeeds with an empty list
given an empty or all-space specialty, when either form is requested, then the result matches a request naming no specialty
given a narrowed list spanning several pages, when the paged directory is shown, then every page link keeps the specialty
given no specialty in the address, when either form is requested, then it lists every veterinarian as before
non_goals: free-text veterinarian search, and pet or visit search (NG-9 as narrowed)
any form, dropdown, or other on-page control for choosing a specialty, on either surface
an on-page indication of the active specialty (open question)
trimming a specialty padded with spaces (open question)
narrowing by more than one specialty per request (open question)
notes: REQ-VET-004 (fresh ID for the reinstated machine-readable list, per the intake decision; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn) is already met by the existing /vets route and its existing test; this slice adds no separate work for it. Edge cases 2-3 of the Veterinarian directory apply: a vet holding several specialties appears once; a vet holding the named one among others is included. Three open questions were recorded in the PRD instead of decided: padded values, an active-specialty indication, and repeated parameters. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope. The system-design.md rows mapping Vets and VetController to no requirement or to REQ-VET-001 alone are now stale for the design expert.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The vet feature package's existing controller-to-repository shape carries the slice (system-design.md § Contracts; feature-package ADR). The paged narrowed read follows the paged derived-query pattern that owner search demonstrates (OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName over OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, located by grep, a weaker basis than the IDE oracle, which is not connected). There are three adjustments. First, VetRepository gains two narrowed reads, one paged and one whole, each matching the specialty's whole name ignoring case and listing each veterinarian once. Second, the narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable (new ADR 2026-09-30-request-keyed-reads-stay-uncached). Third, VetController binds an optional specialty on both routes, treating a blank one as absent. The machine-readable /vets route is now REQ-VET-004 and stays in the Vets wrapper unchanged. Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration now cite REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004. A new § Scale and Load row covers the directory path.
integration_points: Binding (both new entry points: GET /vets.html and GET /vets gain a specialty parameter): bind a request-scoped String via @RequestParam(required = false). No persisted type is bound. Normalization is controller binding (architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Web controller row): null, empty or all-whitespace means absent and calls the existing unnarrowed read. A non-blank value is passed to the repository verbatim, untrimmed, because padded values are an open PRD question and a declared non-goal. No test pins padded or repeated-parameter behavior.

Repository boundary, matching semantics (whole name, letter case, prefix rejection, empty result, each vet once): real implementation, Spring Data JPA over the embedded H2 seed data in the existing @DataJpaTest seam ClinicServiceTests (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: prefer real implementations). The controller's mocked repository cannot prove the query, so these assertions belong here.

Repository boundary, controller tests (binding, blank-as-absent, page links, both routes): VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest whose context already binds VetRepository as a @MockitoBean, and a second repository bean would collide. New controller tests use that existing stub as the recorded exception (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: tolerated existing usage). They verify which read is called with which argument. A multi-page narrowed list is also only reachable this way: seed data holds at most two vets per specialty against a page size of five, and VetRepository has no write path.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-test harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Template: the vetList.html page links (numbered, first, previous, next, last) are built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, for example @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, so the specialty is URL-encoded. The current '__${i}__' string-concatenation form must not carry the specialty. The controller exposes the normalized specialty (absent when blank) as a model attribute. When absent, links carry no specialty parameter.

patterns.description: Paged read helper with a local page size and PageRequest; the narrowed paged read mirrors it, keeping the vet page size a local value.
Blank search input treated as the broadest query. The vet slice treats blank as absent but does not strip a non-blank value.

Existing paged read. The narrowed reads sit beside it as derived queries (for example findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase with a Pageable and a Collection variant) or as explicit parameterized @Query with a matching count query. Either way they carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable.

risks.risk: Letter-case matching diverges by vendor: PostgreSQL stores specialties.name as case-sensitive TEXT (system-design.md § Known Defects shows the same failure in owner search).
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the query on both sides, through a derived IgnoreCase (UPPER on both operands) or LOWER() in explicit JPQL. Never rely on column collation.

risks.risk: A veterinarian is listed twice, or the page count is inflated. Specialty names carry no uniqueness constraint in any vendor schema, so two rows differing only by case both match the join (PRD edge case 2).
risks.mitigation: Select distinct veterinarians. For the paged read the count query must count distinct veterinarians as well; a derived findDistinct... query does this.

risks.risk: Unbounded cache growth keyed on caller-supplied specialty text, on an unauthenticated route (security-principles § Trust Boundaries: fail secure; the vets cache has no size limit).
risks.mitigation: The narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable (ADR 2026-09-30-request-keyed-reads-stay-uncached). The same flaw in the existing page-number key is recorded under § Known Defects and not fixed in this slice.

risks.risk: Injection through the specialty value into the query or into the page-link URL (security-principles § Realization: injection into data access).
risks.mitigation: Pass the value to the query only as a bound parameter, through a derived query or a named parameter; never concatenate it into query text. Page links use encoded Thymeleaf link parameters. The specialty is not echoed as page text, so no new output-escaping surface opens.

risks.risk: Vet directory path, per the § Scale and Load row (Veterinarian directory): data size is unrecorded and treated as bounded.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one parameterized join per narrowed request, uncached. No in-memory filtering of the cached whole list.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Follow-ups from the prd-entry notes are done. docs/adr/README.md now indexes the NG-9 non-goal ADR and the new cache ADR. The Contracts rows for Vets and VetController cite REQ-VET-003/004. The stale known-defect row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less is removed, since REQ-VET-004 reinstates it. docs/system-design.md gained the harness-template § Scale and Load section it lacked, with one row. The Security Context inputs and the SQL-injection threat row are updated. A newly observed pre-existing defect is recorded as derived and unconfirmed: the paged vet read's cache key includes the request's page number. Doctor check passes (0 failures). REQ-VET-004 needs no new code; the existing /vets test covers it.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty value reaches the database only as a bound argument to the Spring Data derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` and `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable)` (VetRepository.java diff hunk @@ -55,4 +55,20 @@). No query text is built from the value, so this meets the security-principles.md row on injection into data access.

XSS and template-expression injection: the request-supplied specialty reaches the page only through Thymeleaf link-parameter syntax, `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}` (vetList.html:30, 35, 40, 45, 50). Link parameters are URL-encoded and th:href attribute-escaped; VetControllerTests.java:173 asserts `specialty=large%20animal` with `&`. The change also removes the old `__${i}__` preprocessing from every page link. A `grep -F -e utext -e '__$'` on vetList.html matches nothing, so no preprocessing or unescaped output remains.

Uncontrolled resource consumption: the new narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable. `grep -F @Cacheable` in the vet package matches only VetRepository.java:45 and :55, the pre-existing unnarrowed reads. Caller-supplied text therefore cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache, which follows the new request-keyed-reads-stay-uncached ADR. The pre-existing unbounded cache keyed on page number is already recorded as a known gap in system-design.md:219. This change leaves it as it was.

Exposed surface: no new route, no new binding target, no @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody, and no new model attribute beyond the echoed, encoded specialty string. The JSON route /vets returns the same `Vets` wrapper, and the request value is not reflected in it. A blank specialty falls back to the existing whole-list read, so there is no error path that could leak exception detail.
The diff adds no secrets, logging, file I/O, process execution, or deserialization entry point.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and jackson-databind 3.1.5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no dependencyCheck task in `./gradlew tasks --all`), so no NVD match was run in this review.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The two trailing `then(this.vets).should(never())...` verifications restate the outcome the test already asserts: both forms return the two unnarrowed vets (`hasSize(2)`, `$.vetList.length()` = 2). If a blank specialty reached the narrowed query, the unstubbed mock would return an empty result and those assertions would fail. The interaction is not itself the contract here (test-review Mocking Policy: no verify restating an outcome). The unused imports `then`, `never`, `anyString` go with them.
findings.fix: Delete the two `never()` verifications and the imports only they use (`then`, `never`, `anyString`).

recommendations: Not verified in this review: the paged form's case-insensitivity and prefix behavior. Only the whole (Collection) overload is tested for those two cases. The paged overload is a separate derived query, so a paged-only test for one of them would pin bullets 3 and 4 for 'either form'.

The page-link test pins the encoding only for a space ('large%20animal'). A specialty with reserved characters such as '&' or '<' would pin that the link parameters are escaped, since the value is user-supplied and echoed into hrefs.

theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyListWhenNoVetHoldsIt stubs the mock to return empty and asserts empty, so it exercises only the controller's pass-through. The real 'no vet holds it' behavior has no repository-level test; the prefix test is the nearest. A repository test for an unknown specialty would catch a real query change.

The ClinicServiceTests assertions pick `Vet::getLastName` with the seed literals 'Douglas' and 'Ortega' repeated four times. Naming them as constants (or comparing loaded entities) would follow the brief's whole-object and Tier 3 conventions.
approved_aspects: Placement matches the design: the query semantics (whole name, ignore case, each vet once, paged and whole) are tested at the repository seam in ClinicServiceTests, and binding, blank handling and page links at the web layer with MockMvc (system-design.md VetRepository and VetController rows).

The one declared name with no match, theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameIgnoringCase, is covered by theVetSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchIgnoringLetterCase plus theVetSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchOnlyTheStartOfAName. The edge case of a vet holding the specialty among others is covered by the Douglas seed row (Douglas is expected under 'surgery').

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Scope: fix-delta against ca92a6e5 (`python3 scripts/changeset.py --base-tree ca92a6e59c45684058741e2a26133bc22b4878be --name-only` lists docs/system-design.md, vetList.html, and VetControllerTests.java). VetController.java and VetRepository.java are not in the delta, so the parameterized derived-query path approved in round 1 is unchanged.

Pagination links in the reworked template: the request-supplied specialty is now concatenated onto the link as `'&specialty=' + ${#uris.escapeQueryParam(specialty)}` (vetList.html:27). Thymeleaf's standard #uris query-param escaping (unbescape 1.1.6.RELEASE) percent-encodes the value. The fixed `&specialty=` prefix cannot be turned into a new parameter or a fragment. The whole th:href value then gets HTML attribute escaping on output. VetControllerTests.java:168 asserts `/vets.html?page=1&specialty=large%20animal`. Every href starts with the context-relative `@{/vets.html(...)}`, so a request value cannot supply a scheme such as `javascript:`. Not verified in this review: that the escaper encodes `&`, `=` and `#` specifically. No test feeds those characters and I did not run the escaper. At worst, an unencoded `&` would add a parameter to a same-origin link to the read-only /vets.html route, which binds only `page` and `specialty`.
No template preprocessing or unescaped output was reintroduced. `grep -F -e utext -e '__$'` on vetList.html matches nothing.

The docs/system-design.md delta is prose only (Scale and Load preamble) and has no security surface. The VetControllerTests.java delta removes Mockito `never()` interactions on the blank-specialty test. Those assertions pinned a routing choice, not a security control: both read paths are parameterized and the narrowed one is uncached. Removing them weakens no guard.
The delta adds no secrets, logging, file I/O, process execution, request-binding target, or deserialization entry point.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the delta. The resolved framework versions stand as recorded in round 1: Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and jackson-databind 3.1.5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match was run. `./gradlew test` was not re-run in this pass because the build-pass at line 20 covers the tree.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet list by specialty on /vets.html and /vets

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the vet package (controller, repository with two new derived queries, list template) plus PRD, design and ADR docs; no sensitive paths, one module, existing no-specialty paths preserved.

semantic_surprise.note: The round-2 fix delta rebuilt the page links as string concatenation, @{/vets.html(page=...)} + '&specialty=' + #uris.escapeQueryParam(specialty), abandoning the design-block's prescribed Thymeleaf link-parameter form; a user-supplied value is now spliced into hrefs by hand, and the escaping of '&', '=', '#' was explicitly not verified by the security reviewer.
